body:
Independent review of #153 (diff against `issue/103-turning-axial-rapids`, head `d49d7d3`).

## Correctness (Prime Directive): no blocking finding

- **`reads_prior` coverage.** Every reader of the program ahead is inside it: `prior_state` (Pocket3D, MultiAxisRough, which has no tilt, so it is caught by `tilt().is_none()`, and was undigested before this PR), `prior_plan` / `acquit_by_prior` (gated on `frame.is_none()`, which is the same predicate as `tilt().is_none()`, because `collect_job` errors on a tilt with no frame), `drills_ahead` (turning section, never tilted), and the Drill prior (always in). I found no kind left out.
- **`prior_digest` inputs.** Order, deletion, setup move and rename all change the name list. The predecessor's cached path, tool radius, ball, cone, bull corner and nose are hashed. Editing a predecessor without regenerating it does not change the digest, but then the predecessor itself is Stale and `program_ops` refuses the whole post, so nothing stale ships.
- **Rounds.** These converge by induction in program order. The op at position p is final in round p at the latest, so `cap = op count` is enough. An op that fails in a later round keeps its round-1 result with a stamp that no longer matches, so it reads Stale and the post refuses it. A leftover at the cap is Stale and also refused. Construction applies each round and then inverts in reverse. `GenerateOperation::apply` and `invert` only set components (no observers in app/ui), so the world is restored exactly, and replay followed by undo is exact even when the same op appears in two rounds. On the error paths, `stage_generation` and `finish` failures are never applied, so nothing needs inverting.

## BLOCKING

**B1 (perf, user-visible): `status_of` is now quadratic in the job's path sizes, and it runs every frame.**
`reads_prior` widens the `R` digest from {Pocket3D, Drill} to every unposed op. `current_stamp` calls `prior_digest`, which goes through `ahead_of`, and that **clones** each predecessor's whole `Toolpath` (`model::toolpath_of` uses `t.clone()`, warnings included) and then `path_hash`es every move. `status_of` is called for every op on every frame, by the status-bar stale count (`ui/src/egui_app/panes.rs:1242`) and by the browser tree rows (`panes.rs:1495`). On an M-op job that costs M(M-1)/2 full path clones and hashes per call site per frame.
Scenario: 20 unposed ops with 3D or adaptive paths of about 100k moves (Move is over 100 B). That is 190 clones of roughly 10+ MB each, about 2 GB of memcpy and hashing per frame, twice over. Before this PR the cost applied only to Pocket3D/Drill.
`RegenerateAll` pays it too: each round runs `status_of` over every op, then again for the leftover scan, which makes it O(rounds·M²·P).
Fix suggestion: hash the predecessor by reference instead of cloning (`try_get::<&Toolpath>(|t| path_hash(&t.path.moves))`). Better still, compute the path hash once when the cache is written (store it on `Toolpath`, or memoise it per entity the way M5.3 A does for `geometry_signature`). That makes the digest O(M) cheap reads.

## Non-blocking

- **N1 (perf): wasted regeneration in the rounds.** Every unposed op now reads the program ahead, so once the first op's path moves, round 2 regenerates every op behind it a second time. A plain model revision therefore costs about 2× the generation work, and a chain whose paths depend on the prior (rest roughing, acquittal-lifted rapids) can cost up to M(M+1)/2 generations. Possible fix: in a round, defer any op whose same-setup ahead set contains an op staged in that round. That generates each op once, keeps the parallelism across setups, and leaves the verdict unchanged.
- **N2: the stock is not part of the acquittal's inputs.** `PriorPlan`'s grid comes from `stock_grid`, and the raw-stock `RapidInStock` conviction reads the stock too. Neither `prior_digest` nor the stamp of an Entity-sourced, Fixed-height op digests the stock (only `SrcRef::Stock`, the Drill `X` clause and stock-referenced heights do). The post's live gate re-checks rapids only against workholding. So a stock that grows after generation leaves a Contour's rapid verdict Ok without being re-judged. This predates the PR (the raw verdict already had the gap), so it is not a regression here, but it belongs to the same "verdict reads a stale input" class and deserves its own issue.
- **N3:** the predecessor's `kind` is not in `digest_of`, but `prior_plan` (Facing vs other turning) and `drills_ahead` (Drill only) branch on it. A kind change leaves that predecessor Stale until it is regenerated, and its regenerated path differs in practice, so this is safe today. Hashing `kind.info().tag` would make that explicit, since the one-time Stale is already being paid.
- **N4:** an op whose *staging* fails in round 1 because its predecessor is in a bad state is never retried in a later round, even if the predecessor is fixed in that round. It stays Stale (safe) and needs a second click.

## Tests

- The pins are good: they post and assert a named refusal, not just a status. `threaded_batch_matches_the_serial_loop_bit_for_bit` against a sequential generate-and-apply loop is the right oracle.
- Gaps: no test for **reorder** (claimed in the PR body); no test that a **3+2-posed** op's stamp is unchanged (the inert-data claim); no test for a **later-round failure** (op succeeds in round 1 and fails in round 2: stays Stale, post refuses, undo is exact). The undo check in `one_regenerate_all_brings_a_dependent_pair_current` asserts statuses, not bytes; comparing the caches before and after undo would pin "undo is exact".

## Readings

`cargo test -p camcraft-app --test vertical_rapid_stock --test operations` in `cc-issue109`: operations 117 passed (6 ignored), vertical_rapid_stock 6 passed.

Verdict: one blocking item (B1, per-frame perf regression). The staleness and convergence logic is correct.

Review addressed in 5cfeaf7 (pushed to issue/109-stale-prior-acquittal).

- **B1:** `schema::Toolpath` now stores a private path signature (`path_sig::of`, which was `rest::path_hash`). It is computed once in `Toolpath::new`, the only constructor. `prior_digest` and `prior_stale` read it through a borrowed component, so they no longer clone any moves; `status_of` now does one cheap read per op ahead. Only `prior_state`, `prior_plan` and `drills_ahead` still copy moves, because they build the grid at generation. The one test that spliced a cache in place (drilling_cross_rapids) now rebuilds it with `Toolpath::new`. I picked this over a sibling component, which would leave two writers to keep in step, and over an on-set observer (app has none).
- **N3:** the kind tag of each op ahead is now hashed into `digest_of`.
- **N1:** a round now holds back an op that reads the program ahead if an op ahead of it in the same setup is staged in that round. Each op generates once, and different setups still run in parallel.
- **N2:** not done here; it is being filed separately.
- **Tests:** added `the_program_ahead_digest_moves_only_with_the_path` (the digest and signature stay the same on an identical regenerate, stay the same on an edit that is not regenerated, and change when the path moves), `a_reorder_marks_the_dependent_stale` (both ops go Stale and the post refuses) and `a_posed_op_keeps_its_stamp_when_the_program_ahead_moves` (the 3+2 face's stamp does not change, the unposed contour's does).

Results:
- app: lib 72, operations 117 (6 ignored), vertical_rapid_stock 9, turning_bore 11, remachining 6, commands_undo 30, drill_prior 10, drill_prior_kinds 4, drilling_cross_rapids 2, posting 17, tool_after_state 5, project_roundtrip 68 and golden_cl 23 all pass.
- ui (CWD crates/ui): `regenerate_all_fixes_stale_ops_through_the_queue`, `regenerate_all_on_a_current_job_writes_no_history` and `status_bar_offers_regenerate_all_when_something_is_stale` pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Re-review of #153 at head `5cfeaf7`.

## B1 (path signature): resolved

- `Toolpath.sig` is private, so outside `schema.rs` the compiler forces every construction through `Toolpath::new`. The writers I found are generate (`Staged::finish`), delete-undo (`DeleteOperation::invert`), project load (`PathDto::to_cache`, used by `project/apply.rs:673`) and `Default`, and all go through `new`. `GenerateOperation::invert`, `ClearToolpath` and paste set clones of an intact component, so they carry the matching sig.
- `Toolpath` is not `Serialize`/`Deserialize`, and the flecs registration is a plain `world.component::<Toolpath>()`, so nothing can rebuild it field by field.
- Nothing mutates the cache in place: I searched for `&mut Toolpath`, `get_mut`, and in-place writes to `.path`, `.path.moves` and `.warnings` outside tests, and found none. An edited cache with an old sig is not reachable today.
- `ahead_of(.., false)` reads `path_sig()` through a borrowed `try_get::<&Toolpath>` and clones nothing. Only `prior_state`, `prior_plan` and `drills_ahead` copy moves, and they run at generation, not every frame.
- `path_sig::of` hashes the same bytes as the old `path_hash`.
- Nit: `path` is still a `pub` field, so a future `get_mut` that edits it in place would leave `sig` stale without any compiler error. Consider a getter-only `path`, or a test or doc rule.

## N3 (kind hashed): resolved

`digest_of` now writes `kind.info().tag` for every predecessor.

## N1 (deferral): staleness is correct, but it introduces one regression

On staleness the deferral is sound. A reads-prior op is staged only when nothing ahead of it in its setup is staged that round. So everything ahead is final when it runs, each op generates once, and the rounds needed are at most the stale-op count, which the cap allows for.

**BLOCKING: one broken op now stops Regenerate All from regenerating every reads-prior op behind it in the same setup.**
`new()` breaks out of the loop when `round()` returns no parts. But `round()` returns only the jobs that *finished*: a job that stages but fails in `finish` (a `run_job` `GenError`) is pushed to `skipped` and contributes no part, while the ops it deferred are never staged.
Scenario: the part is revised (`UpdateModel`), so `Pocket1` and `Contour2`, both unposed and in one setup, go Stale. `Pocket1` stages, and then its generator refuses (for example, the tool no longer fits the revised pocket). `Contour2` was deferred behind it. The round yields zero parts, the loop breaks, and `Contour2` is never regenerated. It is reported as `"still stale after N regeneration round(s)"` even though only one round ran.
- Before this commit, `Contour2` was regenerated in round 1. That breaks the law in `RegenerateAll`'s own doc comment: "one broken pick must not block the rest of the job."
- The existing failure tests (`operations.rs` ~1300, `tool_after_state`) fail at *staging* (tool gate). A staging failure never enters `staged_setups`, so they don't catch this.
- It is safe for the Prime Directive (the post refuses the Stale ops either way), but every op behind one refusal is left unregenerated, with a wrong explanation.
- Fix: stop the loop only when a round *staged* nothing, not when nothing *succeeded*. One way is to have `round()` also report whether it staged anything. Pin it with a test where the first op fails in `finish` and a dependent behind it ends up Ok after one Regenerate All.

## Readings

At `5cfeaf7` in `cc-issue109`: operations 117 passed (6 ignored), vertical_rapid_stock 9 passed, tool_after_state 5 passed.

Verdict: B1 and N3 are clean. One blocking regression is in the N1 deferral: the loop stops early when a staged op fails in `finish`.

Re-review blocker fixed in bc8324f (pushed).

- **N1 regression:** the rounds loop now stops only when a round *staged* nothing. `round()` returns `(parts, staged_any)`, and staged_any also counts ops refused at staging. A refusal is final, because the refused op is in `skipped` and excluded from later rounds, so the ops it held back run in the next round against the current world. The "still stale after N round(s)" message now counts the rounds actually run, and it can only fire at the cap.
- **Pin:** `a_refused_op_ahead_does_not_hold_back_the_ops_behind_it` (vertical_rapid_stock). A staged Face measured from the stock top goes Stale when the block grows past its Z 20 clearance, and its generator refuses in `finish` ("clearance plane not above the first cut level"). Before the fix the result was `["Op1Face: ... clearance plane not above the first cut level", "Op2Contour: still stale after 2 regeneration round(s)"]` with 0 ops regenerated. Now the contour is the one op regenerated and reads Ok, only the face's refusal is named, and the face keeps its Stale tag.
- **`Toolpath.path` accessor:** skipped. Making it private touches about 78 files. The type doc states the rule instead: a cache is rebuilt whole through `Toolpath::new` and never edited in place.

Results:
- app: lib 72, operations 117 (6 ignored), vertical_rapid_stock 10, turning_bore 11, remachining 6, commands_undo 30, drill_prior 10, posting 17 and tool_after_state 5 all pass.
- ui (CWD crates/ui): the two `regenerate_all` queue tests and `status_bar_offers_regenerate_all_when_something_is_stale` pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Re-check of #153 at head `bc8324f`: **clean, no blocking items.**

- **N1 regression fixed.** The rounds loop now stops only when a round *attempted* nothing (staged, or refused at staging). An op refused in `finish` is in `skipped`, and later rounds exclude it, so the ops deferred behind it are staged in the next round.
- **Termination and cap.** Every attempted round either applies at least one op or adds at least one to `skipped`. A deferral can only happen when something else was staged in that round, so the loop cannot spin on an empty round. An op is staged only once nothing ahead of it in its setup is moving, so it stays Ok after apply. That bounds the rounds by the stale-op count, which is at most `cap`. The leftover message now counts the rounds actually run.
- **Pin.** `a_refused_op_ahead_does_not_hold_back_the_ops_behind_it` is a real pin. The face's refusal comes from the motion face generator (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/face.rs`), so it fires in `finish`, not at staging. That is exactly the path that used to stop the loop early. The test asserts that the contour regenerates and reads Ok, and that only the face is named, with no "still stale" text.
- **`Toolpath.path`.** The doc note ("written whole, never edited in place") is acceptable. I still find no in-place writer today.

Readings at `bc8324f` in `cc-issue109`: operations 117 passed (6 ignored), vertical_rapid_stock 10 passed, tool_after_state 5 passed.

Merged origin/main (#135, #149, and #103's final changes) in 9fffe3c; the turning case is pinned in 91b994c. Both are pushed.

- **rest.rs conflict:** I took #149's split. The ahead walk and the digest now live in `rest/ahead.rs`, and that is where this PR's changes went: `ahead_of(.., with_moves)` reads the stored `path_sig()` without a clone, and the kind tag is hashed. The old `path_hash` was removed in favour of `path_sig::of`. `turned_ahead` (#159), which is new from main, passes `with_moves = true`.
- **turning_bore conflict:** the fixture still lives in `tests/common/bore.rs`, now with #103's final values (the Ø11.2 pilot, radius 5.65).
- **Turning case:** `a_rough_moved_after_deleted_or_made_shallower_stales_its_finish` (lathe_post) runs R1 rough then S1 finish. For each of R1 reordered after S1, R1 deleted, and R1 re-cut shallower (bottom Z 10) and regenerated, S1 reads Stale and the post refuses.
- **Existing test changed:** `a_finish_posted_ahead_of_its_rough_is_convicted_by_name` now creates P1 before R1. R1 sorts behind P1 and digests it (#109), so in the old creation order R1 read Stale and the post refused it before reaching P1's rapid.

Results:
- app: lib 74, operations 117 (6 ignored), vertical_rapid_stock 10, turning_bore 11, turning_contour 10, lathe_post 7, remachining 6, drill_prior 10, stock_stamp 4, posting 17, golden_cl 23, commands_undo 30 and tool_after_state 5 all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
